rv.q: And it’s in expressing Willy’s disintegrating mental state that Pierce truly excels. He is by turns frightened, affectionate, furious and lost, feelings moving through his face and body like waves. But Clarke is just as good: soft with Willy, pitiless with her feckless sons.
Despite its often-dreamy pace, these carefully observed moments mean that ‘Death of a Salesman’ has a real urgency to it.

Marianne Elliot and Miranda Cromwell’s extraordinary revival of Arthur Miller’s classic mints the play fresh, it looks as if it was written today, for our times, and is one of the most moving experiences I’ve had in the theatre this year.
People will be talking about it for years to come.
It's emotionally draining but entirely worth it.

cn.t: Critics hail this production as a triumph that enhances Miller's masterpiece, with powerhouse performances from Wendell Pierce and Sharon D Clarke earning widespread acclaim in this resonant revival.
